summaries.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI is the AWS service for custom model training, fine-tuning and hosting. Serverless model customization (SFT, DPO, RFT, LoRA, full fine-tuning) launched in December 2025, and training session APIs followed in October 2026, available in us-east-1, us-west-2, ap-northeast-1 and eu-west-1. Execution roles trust sagemaker.amazonaws.com and are passed with iam:PassRole; AmazonSageMakerFullAccess is the broad managed policy. Pricing is pay-as-you-go.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the cloud vendor behind IAM, Bedrock, AgentCore, Lambda, Step Functions and EventBridge, all reached through HTTPS APIs and SDKs rather than JDBC or ODBC drivers. An engineer joining an AWS client should ask on day one for an Identity Center user and permission set, the target Regions and any Region-deny SCP, completed Bedrock model prerequisites, model quotas, VPC details, and IdP details for AgentCore JWT auth. Docs offer a site-wide llms.txt.

The ant CLI is Anthropic's command-line tool for the Claude API, currently version 2.9.0. Sign in with ant auth login; adding --scope org:admin gets an Admin API token, and ant auth status shows which credential won precedence. It installs via Homebrew, a GitHub release tarball or go install, and there is no native Windows installer (use go install or WSL). It does not support Bedrock or Google managed Claude.

Anthropic is the AI company behind Claude. It runs Claude Console at platform.claude.com for API organizations and sells Claude through partners such as Microsoft Foundry, where it is seller and independent data processor. Its commercial terms bar training on customer content. Attestations include SOC 2 Type I and II, ISO 27001, ISO/IEC 42001 and HIPAA-ready configuration. Claude Fable 5.2 is among its latest models, and retirements get at least 60 days' notice.

Anthropic Claude models are offered through many platforms, including Microsoft Foundry, Google Model Garden, Databricks, Snowflake Cortex and Salesforce. In Foundry they bill through Azure Marketplace in Claude Consumption Units, need a pay-as-you-go subscription in an eligible country, and come in Azure-hosted or Anthropic-hosted versions. On Google Cloud each model must be enabled in Model Garden, with lineage-shared quotas for newer models. Claude 5.5 models became GA in Snowflake Cortex on 2026-11-06.

The Anthropic client SDKs are Anthropic's official libraries for the Claude API, with major releases on 2026-10-21 (Python 2.0.0, TypeScript 1.0.0) moving to API version 2026-10-21 and Apache 2.0. They expose the Admin API under client.organization, a tool runner, MCP conversion helpers, and default retries on connection errors, 429 and 5xx. Platform-specific packages cover Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Versions are published in sdk-versions.json.

The anthropic[vertex] SDK is Anthropic's Python SDK extra for calling Claude on Google's Agent Platform. Install it with pip install -U 'anthropic[vertex]' and use the AnthropicVertex client with a project ID and region; the anthropic package was at 2.8.0 on PyPI as of 2026-11-10. Claude on Agent Platform supports client tools (function calling), but Google's page says server tools are not supported.

Antigravity CLI (agy) is Google's command-line agent, launched 2026-05-19 with Antigravity 2.0. It replaced Gemini CLI for personal, Google AI Pro and Ultra users from 2026-06-18. Auth types are oauth-personal, oauth-business (Gemini Enterprise, preview), gemini-api-key and agent-platform (preview); session tokens move into the OS keyring. Migration moves MCP config and skills into new locations, and agy plugin import gemini converts extensions. Whether a free tier exists is unconfirmed.

API Access Control is a Salesforce security setting that limits API access to allowlisted connected apps that are installed and unblocked, with access granted only to users whose profile or permission set is tied to the app. Some orgs must ask Salesforce Support to enable it. Since the week of 2025-12-08 the Use Any API Client permission still bypasses it but no longer lets users self-authorize uninstalled apps. Third-party tools such as DBAmp have broken under it.

The Apigee API hub MCP server is Google Cloud's managed MCP endpoint for Apigee API hub, GA since 2026-07-24, with global and regional endpoints. It integrates with Model Armor, and API hub syncs MCP metadata to Agent Registry by default, which matters for agent tool discovery and governance.

The Apigee MCP Discovery Proxy is Google Cloud Apigee's way to host MCP servers for existing APIs: each OpenAPI 3.0.x operation becomes an MCP tool, authenticated with OAuth 2.1 or OIDC. It runs on Subscription, Pay-as-you-go, Evaluation and Data Residency orgs and on Apigee hybrid 1.17.0 or later. SaaS orgs are capped at 1,000 tools, SSE isn't supported, and provisioning may fail in a few European and Middle East regions.

Application Default Credentials (ADC) is Google Cloud's standard credential lookup for client libraries, ADK, Gemini CLI and MCP clients. It searches GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then the gcloud ADC file created by gcloud auth application-default login, then an attached service account. MCP clients add an x-goog-user-project header, and ADC user tokens expire about every hour. Gemini Enterprise API access also uses ADC or gcloud bearer tokens.

Application Integration is Google Cloud's workflow integration service, reachable from ADK through ApplicationIntegrationToolset to expose workflows and Integration Connectors as agent tools. The MCP connector is used from it via the Connectors task. On 2026-08-28 Google announced a change to how identities are handled for integration runs that may require customer action.

The Autonomous AI Database A2A Server is an Oracle feature that publishes Select AI agent teams as A2A agents, discoverable through Agent Cards. It is built in and multi-tenant for 26ai and 19c on Serverless and Dedicated Region, uses OAuth with database credentials, and is enabled separately from the MCP Server. Its release date, endpoint URL and enablement steps are unconfirmed.

The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server is Oracle's managed remote MCP server, one per database, for 26ai and 19c, GA since December 2025. It serves Streamable HTTP, private endpoints are reachable only from the VCN, and it is enabled in the Console under Tool configuration. Auth is OAuth dynamic or static client registration, or a one-hour bearer token from database credentials. Tools are Select AI Agent tools filtered by the DB user's privileges.

AWS Agent Registry (formerly AgentCore Registry) is AWS's governed catalog of MCP servers, agents, skills and tools, with approval workflows, hybrid search and a native MCP endpoint. It has been GA since August 2026 after an April 2026 preview. AWS Quick can enable MCP servers and agents from it, and it reached AWS GovCloud (US-West) on 2026-11-06.

The AWS CLI is AWS's command-line tool, with v2 at 2.40.3 (2026-11-13). On Windows install it via the signed PowerShell script or MSIs; a winget package exists but isn't in AWS docs. For local dev, aws login with console credentials is recommended (auto-refresh up to 12 hours); aws configure sso sets up Identity Center sign-in, with PKCE as default since 2.22.0. It also handles Bedrock model agreements and outbound federation enablement.

AWS IAM Identity Center is AWS's human SSO layer, federating an external IdP over SAML and provisioning users and groups over SCIM 2.0 from Okta or Microsoft Entra ID. Permission sets become an IAM role in each assigned account, and engineers joining an AWS client should ask for a user and permission set in the target accounts. Trusted identity propagation carries end-user identity to AWS services. Amazon Q Developer Pro requires an instance.

IAM outbound identity federation, announced 2025-11-19, lets AWS workloads authenticate to other clouds and SaaS such as Entra without stored secrets, at no extra cost. It is enabled per account; a principal with sts:GetWebIdentityToken gets an AWS-signed JWT lasting 60 to 3600 seconds (default 300). Condition keys can restrict audience, duration and signing algorithm, and the tokens can't be used to federate back into AWS.

AWS Knowledge MCP Server is AWS's remote, no-auth, rate-limited documentation MCP server, GA since October 2025, offering tools to search and read docs, get recommendations, and check Region availability. It needs no AWS account. AWS now recommends the AWS MCP Server instead, and its setup guide says to remove this server to avoid overlapping tools.

AWS Lambda is AWS's serverless compute service and the usual glue for agent tools, for example EventBridge to Lambda to InvokeAgentRuntime for event-driven AgentCore agents. Execution roles trust lambda.amazonaws.com, and Bedrock Agents action-group functions need a resource policy allowing Bedrock. Limits include a 900-second timeout, 6 MB synchronous payloads and default concurrency of 1,000 per Region. Durable functions add checkpointed workflows that can wait up to a year.

AWS Marketplace is AWS's software storefront and billing channel. The first Bedrock model call sets up a Marketplace subscription, and missing prerequisites can cause AccessDeniedException up to 15 minutes later. Private offers should be accepted from the management account or a delegated admin, and member accounts pay public rates until License Manager grants exist. Databricks, Oracle Database@AWS and ChatGPT Enterprise are also sold through it.

AWS MCP Server is AWS's managed remote MCP server, part of the Agent Toolkit for AWS and GA since 2026-05-06, at no extra charge. One endpoint lets agents call any AWS API, run sandboxed Python, read docs and load skills, with IAM guardrails and CloudTrail logging. Auth is OAuth 2.1 through AWS Sign-in or SigV4 via the MCP Proxy for AWS. The setup guide lists eight Regions, and rate limits are fixed at 10 requests per second per account per Region.

AWS Organizations is AWS's account hierarchy: one root, one management account, member accounts and nested OUs. Client engagements usually get dedicated workload accounts because quotas are per account per Region. SCPs and RCPs cap IAM permissions, declarative policies also bind the management account, and centralized root access removes member root credentials. A Bedrock policy can enforce a guardrail on every model call across OUs or accounts.

AWS PrivateLink provides private interface VPC endpoints into AWS services. Bedrock has endpoints for bedrock, bedrock-runtime, bedrock-mantle, bedrock-agent and bedrock-agent-runtime, with endpoint policies that can limit actions and principals. AgentCore has data plane, control plane and Gateway endpoints. Databricks on AWS also uses front-end and back-end PrivateLink for private connectivity.

AWS Quick (renamed from Amazon Quick in November 2026, formerly Quick Suite and QuickSight) is AWS's business-user agent workspace with chat, autonomous and always-on agents, flows, apps and deep research; Quick Sight remains its BI part. It acts as an MCP client with OAuth discovery, has built-in SaaS action connectors, and can enable MCP servers and agents from AWS Agent Registry. It's billed per user per month plus a $250 per-account fee.

AWS SigV4 is AWS's request-signing scheme for IAM-authenticated API calls. Claude Platform on AWS uses it with service name aws-external-anthropic, and the Bedrock bedrock-mantle endpoint accepts it or bearer tokens. AWS recommends SigV4 with STS credentials over Bedrock API keys. AgentCore Gateways and Runtimes accept either SigV4 or OAuth JWT inbound auth, chosen at creation.

AWS Step Functions is AWS's workflow orchestration service, priced pay-as-you-go. The console builds least-privilege, Region-scoped roles for Bedrock integrations. An optimized integration invokes the AgentCore harness, but it is request-response only, returns only the final assistant text, and caps the Task state at 900 seconds while the harness keeps running after a timeout.

aws-marketplace:Subscribe is the AWS IAM permission a caller needs to activate a Bedrock model on first invocation. It can be limited to specific models with the aws-marketplace:ProductId condition. A subscription made in one Region makes the model requestable in all offered Regions, even where Subscribe is denied. The account administrator or IAM team usually grants it.

awslabs/mcp is AWS Labs' Apache-2.0 open-source suite of 63 local MCP servers, most run with uvx over stdio. SSE transport was removed on 2025-05-26. Its README calls the Agent Toolkit for AWS the successor for production, and several servers are deprecated in favor of AWS MCP Server.

The azd ai extensions are Microsoft extensions to the Azure Developer CLI for building Foundry agents, installed with azd extension install. They add command groups for agent init, run, invoke, eval, publish and more, plus connections, toolboxes, skills and routines, and define agents in azure.yaml. The azure.ai.agents extension is at version 1.1.0 (2026-11-12).

Azure AI Search is Microsoft's search and retrieval service, underlying Foundry IQ and storing vector stores in Foundry standard setup. New services default to key auth and must switch to RBAC or Both, otherwise token requests are denied; a key wins over a token. Data roles Search Index Data Reader and Contributor grant query and load. Indexers behind private endpoints need a Private execution environment or they fail silently.

Azure AI Search agentic retrieval is Microsoft's knowledge-base retrieval feature for agents, queryable through a retrieve action or an MCP endpoint. GA features use REST API 2026-04-01, while LLM query planning, answer synthesis and multi-turn messages need 2026-08-01-preview; the portals expose only preview schemas. Billing hits two services: Azure AI Search for retrieval tokens and Azure OpenAI for query-planning tokens.

Azure API Management (APIM) is Microsoft's API gateway and the basis of the Foundry AI gateway. It validates inbound Entra tokens and uses managed identity to reach Foundry or Azure OpenAI backends. It can expose REST APIs as remote MCP servers (tools only, no workspaces), front existing MCP servers, and import A2A agent APIs. Response-body logging breaks MCP servers, and GA status of MCP and A2A features is unconfirmed.

The Azure API Management AI gateway is a set of APIM capabilities for LLM APIs, available in all tiers. It adds token limits, token metrics, semantic caching with Azure Managed Redis, content safety, logging, load balancing and a circuit breaker. It supports OpenAI, Anthropic Messages (v2 tiers) and Vertex AI APIs, and a version integrated into Microsoft Foundry is in preview.

The Azure CLI is Microsoft's command-line tool for Azure, currently 2.92.0, installed on Windows with winget, an MSI or a ZIP. Sign in with az login as a user, service principal or managed identity, and get tokens with az account get-access-token. MFA has been required for user identities since September 2025. It assigns roles such as Foundry Agent Consumer that the portal can't, and stores credentials under the user's .azure folder.

Azure Databricks is Databricks on Microsoft Azure, billed through the Azure subscription. The first workspace in an Entra tenant creates the account, and an Entra Global Administrator must set the first account admin. Creating workspaces needs Contributor or Owner at subscription level or a custom role, and those roles also grant workspace admin on first login. The account console isn't available in Azure Government.

The Azure Developer CLI (azd) is Microsoft's developer workflow tool for provisioning and deploying Azure apps, currently 1.37.3. Install on Windows with winget, choco or a PowerShell script; it bundles GitHub CLI and Bicep. azd auth login supports device code, federated credentials and managed identity. Core commands are init, up, provision, deploy and down, and the azd ai extensions add Foundry agent commands.

The Azure Functions MCP extension is Microsoft's binding that turns a function app into a remote MCP server, with tool, resource and prompt triggers plus MCP Apps in C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Java. It serves streamable HTTP with SSE deprecated, and endpoints need the mcp_extension system key by default. Built-in MCP OAuth with Entra and self-hosted MCP SDK servers are still preview, and the extension's GA date is unconfirmed.

Azure Logic Apps is Microsoft's workflow service, which supports autonomous and conversational agentic workflows that use its 1,400+ connectors as tools (Standard GA, Consumption preview). Agent loops use Foundry models or Azure OpenAI, and agents can't be nested as tools. Standard enables a system-assigned managed identity by default. Production chat clients need Easy Auth or Entra OAuth, and custom connectors allow 500 requests per minute per connection.

Azure managed identity is Microsoft's free, secretless workload identity for Azure resources. It lets services such as Logic Apps, the Azure CLI, azd and remote Azure MCP Server authenticate without stored credentials. Role assignments to a managed identity can take several hours to apply because its tokens are cached.

Azure management groups are Microsoft Azure's governance hierarchy above subscriptions, where RBAC and Azure Policy assignments inherit downward. A directory supports up to 10,000 management groups, six levels deep, each with one parent and one trusted Entra tenant. No one has default access to the root management group; only an Entra Global Administrator can elevate access to it.

Azure Marketplace is Microsoft's commercial channel for third-party offers on Azure. Foundry partner and community models such as Anthropic Claude are Marketplace offers treated as Non-Microsoft Products, with Claude billed in Claude Consumption Units. Oracle Database@Azure is bought by accepting a private offer there and linking an OCI tenancy.

Azure MCP Server is Microsoft's open-source MCP server in microsoft/mcp, covering 50+ Azure service namespaces. The latest stable release is 3.0.0; the npm latest tag points to a 4.0 beta, so pin 3.0.0 for stable. Local mode uses a credential chain ending in interactive browser, and remote HTTP mode uses On-Behalf-Of or managed identity with an Entra app scope. Elicitation guards secret-returning tools, and telemetry is on by default.

summaries.key: azure openai in microsoft foundry models
summaries.summary: Azure OpenAI (Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry Models) is OpenAI models sold by Microsoft under Azure identity, billing and compliance, without data shared with OpenAI; it is available up to DoD IL6. Quota is TPM per subscription, region, model and deployment type, moving to shared pools after 2026-05-07, with RPM enforced over short windows. Viewing quota needs Cognitive Services Usages Reader, and deleted resources hold quota 48 hours unless purged.

The Azure RBAC Contributor role is Microsoft Azure's broad management role. On the subscription it covers the Marketplace and SaaS permissions to buy Foundry partner models and to create Azure Databricks workspaces, also granting Databricks workspace admin on first login. It carries no Foundry data actions, so it can't create agents or call agent endpoints. Foundry MCP Server requires Contributor or higher on the project.

The Azure RBAC Owner role is Microsoft Azure's top management role. On the subscription it covers the permissions to buy Foundry partner models and grants Azure Databricks workspace admin on first login. Like Contributor, it can create Foundry accounts, projects and deployments but has no Foundry data actions, so it can't create agents or call agent endpoints.

Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is Microsoft Azure's control plane at management.azure.com, called with api-version query parameters, for example to create Foundry project connections or check Azure OpenAI quota and model capacity. Create, update and delete calls to it fall under mandatory MFA Phase 2 from 2025-10-01.

BigQuery is Google Cloud's data warehouse. Least-privilege access for agent runtime identities pairs roles/bigquery.jobUser (project level or higher) with roles/bigquery.dataViewer on specific datasets. Its managed AI functions (AI.IF, AI.CLASSIFY, AI.SCORE) and general-purpose functions (AI.GENERATE, AI.GENERATE_TABLE) call Agent Platform models and incur their charges.

The BigQuery remote MCP server is Google Cloud's managed MCP endpoint for BigQuery, offering six dataset, table and SQL tools over Streamable HTTP. Using it needs roles/mcp.toolUser, roles/bigquery.jobUser and roles/bigquery.dataViewer; only execute_sql can write, and an IAM deny policy can block it. Queries cancel after 3 minutes by default and return at most 3,000 rows.

The ChatGPT Compliance API is OpenAI's audit export for ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu workspaces, streaming append-only records such as auth logs, conversation messages and Codex logs. It uses an Enterprise Compliance API key and takes a workspace or API Platform organization ID. It is for audit and investigation, not adoption measurement, which belongs to analytics tools.

ChatGPT developer mode is OpenAI's way to add custom MCP servers to ChatGPT, now under ChatGPT Plugins with 'Add custom MCP server', using SSE or streaming HTTP and OAuth, no auth or mixed auth. OAuth registration uses static credentials, CIMD or DCR. These servers are labeled elevated risk, and tools without readOnlyHint count as write actions needing confirmation. Plan eligibility is unconfirmed.

ChatGPT Enterprise is OpenAI's enterprise ChatGPT offering, delivered as a workspace and also sold through AWS Marketplace. It adds SCIM, EKM, analytics, domain verification and RBAC on top of Business's SAML SSO and MFA. Rollout starts with owners, workspace access and identity, then requirements.toml runtime policy. Day-one asks include the right seat, a role granting needed features, plugin enablement, and a service account or token rights; residency details are unconfirmed.

ChatGPT plugins are OpenAI's admin-governed extensions for ChatGPT workspaces, replacing custom GPTs, which become read-only when migrated. In Admin console, admins set each plugin as available, installed, role-customized or disabled, and control app access, read versus write tools and confirmation prompts. Separate member permissions govern using, uploading, sharing, publishing and creating plugins, including those with custom MCP servers.

ChatGPT plugins and Apps SDK is OpenAI's MCP-based developer platform: a plugin bundles skills and/or an MCP server with optional UI, sharing one directory across ChatGPT and Codex. Docs moved to developers.openai.com/plugins, and submission goes through ChatGPT Directory review. UI is a ui:// MCP app resource linked from tools, built with the Model Context Protocol ext-apps and SDK packages.

A ChatGPT service account is OpenAI's non-human workspace identity for Codex automation, available only on pay-as-you-go plans and created only by workspace owners or admins. It runs codex exec with CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, needing Codex CLI 0.142.0 or later. Accounts can be provisioned through SCIM or the Admin API with service_account scopes, and sharing roles are User, Configure and Manager.
